title: Maintenance in Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable (FI-CA)
raw_text:

also exists as business partner in the system where FI-CA runs. CRM middleware replicates the business partner Clerk and makes
the assignment to the contract account.

Maintenance in Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable (FI-CA)

In FI-CA, enter the required clerk in the contract accounts of your business partners on the tab page General Data in the field
Clerk Responsible.

Maintenance in CRM System

mySAP CRM portrays the clerk as a partner function using the business agreement. In Customizing for CRM you define which
partner function is to be replicated in the corresponding field in the contract account.

Deleting Data Records No Longer Required

You can delete old entries that are no longer required — this decreases the burden on the system. To do this, on the SAP Easy
Access screen, choose: |}Periodic Processing » Delete Data » Entries in Dunning Telephone List ». See the report
documentation.

Activities
Make the following settings in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable:

e Configure the dunning activities under |)}Business Transactions » Dunning Notices

e Your clerks can use customer contacts to document communication with the business partners in the system. To enable

this, carry out the contact configurations for the program context SAPLFKKDUTL under |)*Basic Functions » Customer
Contacts » Define Configurations

e Under |}Technical Settings » Prepare Processing of Clarification Worklists 5, you can adjust the functions of the
clarification worklist. The relevant application object has the key DUTL. In particular, here you can define your own
processing status and user commands. SAP delivers the function module FKKDUTL_EVENT_UCOMEXIT_OTHER as an

example for user commands.

e If you use the function module FKK_SAMPLE_0746_TEL_ITEM as a dunning activity, you can also create a telephone list in
Correspondence Dunning (compare Dunning Incoming Correspondence).

Dunning History

In a dunning history, the system records all dunning data for each dunned item. There you can find out about the individual
dunning steps. The dunning program uses the dunning history to determine the dunning levels.

In the dunning history (transaction FPM3), you can see which items have been dunned for a particular area. The functions of the
dunning history are protected by the following authorization objects:

e F_KKDU (Dunning in Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable)
e F_KKKO_BUK (Authorization in Company Code)

e F_KKKO_GSB (Authorization in Business Area)
